xavier-becerra.text: Would declare a state of emergency to fund 40,000 already-approved affordable housing units, push cities to zone more residential land for apartments, duplexes and condos, and crack down on cities that make building harder.
Supports expanding down payment assistance for homebuyers and policies to stop large corporations from buying homes en masse.

Would create an ongoing state funding stream for rental assistance and other services and a public dashboard tracking state-funded units; says "people should not be allowed to voluntarily stay on the street when offered shelter" but stopped short of endorsing arrests.
Supports a progressive income tax and extending the higher rate on high earners to fund schools; opposes the billionaire wealth tax (Prop 40); has not ruled out raising taxes.
Open to revising state clean-energy goals "if they make gas and energy unaffordable"; has questioned the 2035 gas-car ban.

Pledges California remains a sanctuary state, local police will not cooperate with immigration enforcement, and universal Medi-Cal for undocumented immigrants continues: "As long as you work hard, obey the law, and pay your taxes in California, as governor, I want you here."

source.title: Democrat Xavier Becerra leverages experience, immigrant roots in bid for California governor (Times of San Diego)

xavier-becerra.text: Previously supported single-payer; now backs expanding state coverage, cutting insurers' administrative spending, requiring more telehealth coverage, and a state loan-repayment fund to recruit health care workers.
Voted for Proposition 36 (2024 tougher-on-crime measure); supports court-mandated drug treatment to avoid jail; opposes longer, stricter sentences generally.
Promises to freeze residential insurance rates and to take regulatory steps to lower electricity and gasoline costs.

source.title: Democrat Xavier Becerra leverages experience, immigrant roots in bid for California governor (Times of San Diego)

steve-hilton.text: Proposes eliminating state income tax on the first $150,000 of income with a flat rate above that (8% per later reporting); "The quickest, most direct way to get money in people's pockets is for the government to take less out in the first place." Would ask departments to save 5% and cancel high-speed rail.

source.title: Steve Hilton pitches affordability agenda as he tries to close gap in CA governor's race

steve-hilton.text: Would cap government-imposed costs on new homes (average $30,000), cut fees and building regulations to "bring back the starter home," and favors suburban single-family homes over dense apartments.

source.title: Steve Hilton pitches affordability agenda as he tries to close gap in CA governor's race

steve-hilton.text: Wants to stop CEQA litigation from blocking construction; says construction costs are "three or four times" higher in California due to regulations and litigation risk.

source.title: Republican Steve Hilton outlines California governor plans (SF Examiner)

steve-hilton.text: Says "camping on the street...is categorically illegal"; police should clear all encampments; would fund sober housing rather than low-barrier shelters.
Would roll back clean-energy mandates, allow more natural gas and in-state oil production, targeting $3 gasoline; also proposes halving the gas tax and promises to "cut your electric bills in half."

source.title: Steve Hilton pitches affordability agenda as he tries to close gap in CA governor's race

steve-hilton.text: Would overturn California's sanctuary law limiting police cooperation with ICE; says "when I'm governor, I will make sure that all laws are peacefully enforced."

source.title: Republican Steve Hilton outlines California governor plans (SF Examiner)

steve-hilton.text: Would end state Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants and redirect the savings to lowering costs for legal residents; favors market competition and preventing provider consolidation.
Supports phonics instruction, making teacher firing easier, charter conversion petitions, public funds for private-school transfers, and bars transgender youth from girls' school sports.
Supports loosening restrictions on firearm ownership and use; opposes the Prop 40 billionaire wealth tax, calling it "asset seizure."
Would curb labor laws used to sue businesses and cut business registration fees.
